openvpn_endpoint_detected.title: OpenVPN Endpoint Detected
openvpn_endpoint_detected.description: An OpenVPN server is responding to P_CONTROL_HARD_RESET_CLIENT_V2 probes on the target. The exposed VPN endpoint allows authorized users to tunnel into the network — but also presents an attack surface if the OpenVPN daemon has known CVEs or if authentication is weak.
openvpn_endpoint_detected.impact: If TLS auth is disabled, the endpoint accepts the first stage of the handshake from anyone — useful for fingerprinting and exhausting server resources. If certificate-based auth is enabled and private keys are protected, exposure is purely informational. Recent OpenVPN CVEs (CVE-2022-0547, CVE-2023-7235) affect specific older versions.
openvpn_endpoint_detected.remediation: Ensure OpenVPN is upgraded to the latest version. Enable `tls-auth` (HMAC firewall) so unauthenticated handshake probes are silently dropped. Require certificate-based authentication and disable username/password fallback if not needed.
